title: Get — senses & collocations (B1)
note: get is the highest-frequency verb Czech students avoid, because Czech splits its senses across different verbs. Own unit because it is too big for trunk_chunks_b1. Sorted by sense: receive, become, arrive, plus the fixed pairs. First draft 2026-09-02. · 2026-09-04 B1 loop: sentences 8 → 36, one gappable frame per lemma. FIVE of the eight shipped frames could never gap — they used the past or 3sg form (*got a letter*, *got married*, *got a new job*, *got ill*, *gets dark*) while the lemma is the base chunk, so sentenceToFrame found nothing. Every frame here holds its chunk verbatim, which on this pack means the base form of get in every one. E10: Use is use_mode rewrite, 12 underlined paraphrases. F7: *get lost* belongs to leaf_travel_b1 (path 6) and *get on with* to leaf_relationships_b1 (24); replaced with **get wet** and **get over**. · The frames page offered noun frames (I have a … / I need a …) on a pack of verb chunks; they are get-shapes now. · Pool-checked against everything taught before leaf_get_b1 — 0 unknown types.

intro.title: get = arrive, move, and fixed pairs
intro.title_cz: get = dorazit, pohyb a ustálené dvojice

intro.title: You will use these words in
intro.note: Czech uses a different verb for each of these — *dostat*, *stát se*, *dojít*. English uses **get** for all three, and the sense comes from the word after it.
intro.note_cz: Čeština má pro každý význam jiné sloveso. Angličtina má **get** a význam určuje slovo za ním.
